Structure-switching IL-6 aptamers

4 parent aptamers · 1663 ranked ISD switch constructs · 38 single-mismatch variants · 320 negative-control rows · 32 co-folded complexes · constructs built on IL-6-7326.1 (45 nt, truncated) · generated by aptamer/dashboard.py. All data is inlined — works offline except the 3D panel.

Which parent: every construct below is built on IL-6-7326.1, a 45-nt truncation — not on any sequence in the parent table. IL-6-7326.1 is the first 45 nt of the 74-nt IL-6-7326; module B (positions 46–74) is removed, which keeps the finished construct in the length range real E-AB sensors work at. Its published K_D (27 nM) was measured on this truncated form. View 1 shows four full-length parents for reference; the switch library, the mismatch variants and the negative controls all use the 45-mer only.

8 · 3D structures

5 co-folded complexes are inlined here, chosen because they carry the argument: the same DNA chain placed by all four models (view 11's disagreement, in 3D) plus the off-target run that outscores the true target (view 12). Chain A is the protein and chain B the DNA, coloured apart. The other 27 of the 32 predicted structures are not inlined — each .cif is ~250 KB and all of them would add several MB to this page — they are on disk in aptamer/cofold/structures/. These are predictions, not solved structures; see the caveats in views 11–12. This panel loads 3Dmol.js from a CDN, so it is the one view that needs internet.

9 · Mismatch refinement — affinity that costs no tether

Single-mismatch variants of the shortest-tether constructs (38 variants at tether 9–11 nt, all on IL-6-7326.1 (45 nt, truncation of IL-6-7326)). Each row is one variant: the open mark is the unmutated construct's K_D,app, the filled mark is the same construct with one base changed in the displacement strand, and the tether column does not move between them. DS length and linker length both trade affinity against response speed; a mismatch weakens the duplex while leaving both lengths alone, so it is the only knob that improves K_D,app without slowing the sensor. Values are read from mismatches.csv as the pipeline produced them. Not scoped by the filter row above.

30 of 38 passing variants tighten K_D,app, and none of them lengthens the tether. 38 single-mismatch variants of 20 short-tether constructs (tether 9–11 nt). Best overall: 7_3_p1CT, 529 → 124 nM at tether 10 nt. Best of those covering 4 randomised nt: 8_3_p1AT, 938 → 156 nM at tether 11 nt. Matching that 156 nM by lengthening instead — with at least the same 4 randomised nucleotides covered — means a 15-nt tether (DS CAATTCAAC at window 18-26, 137 nM), a 4-nt jump; the tightest such construct anywhere in the library (110 nM, DS AACCCTCTT at window 12-20) pays a 45-nt tether. A longer tether is not free: it slows reclosure and the response, which is why the same affinity bought with a mismatch is worth more than the same affinity bought with linker.
Table view — every passing variant, sortable by any column

10 · Negative controls — does the score detect complementarity or just DNA?

80 designed displacement strands, sampled at a fixed stride across the whole ranked library so the sample is not just its top (of 1663 passing constructs), each against three controls matched to it on length and base composition: scrambled (same bases shuffled), reversed (same bases, wrong pairing register) and foreign (the reverse complement of a window of a shuffled aptamer — a genuine duplex-former that simply is not complementary to this aptamer, and so the strict control). One facet per arm, shared axis; the designed arm is in the accent hue and the controls in grey because the gap between them is the result. Not scoped by the filter row above.

⚠ Caveat 1 — the designed arm's 100% pass rate is partly circular. Those constructs were sampled from switches.csv, which is the set that already passed exactly these filters, so of course they pass again; that number measures nothing. The non-circular evidence is the rest of the figure: the engagement gap (designed median 0.83 against 0.02–0.05 for the controls, with no control exceeding 0.71) and the control pass rates of 0%–4% (scrambled 1%, reversed 4%, foreign 0%) — the controls were never pre-selected for anything, so their failure is a real result and the designed arm's success is not.
⚠ Caveat 2 — the controls still show a negative ΔG_switch, -0.30 to -0.25 kcal/mol at the arm medians. Appending any DNA lowers a construct's free energy, because the tail forms some structure whether or not it is complementary to the aptamer. That residual is exactly the trivial signal that raw ΔG_switch on its own would admit, and the engagement filter (≥ 0.60, the dashed rule) is what excludes it. Read the 0%–4% control pass rate as this pipeline's false-positive floor, not as zero.
Table view — median score and pass rate per arm

Co-folded structures — 32 of 32 predictions, 4 models, 6 DNA chains

Read from aptamer/cofold/, which this page never writes. Views 11 and 12 are not scoped by the switch filter row: the co-folding step ran against its own snapshot of the library.

These are figures and a hypothesis. They are not ranking input, and nothing below feeds the pipeline's ranking. The ranking comes from switches.csv — thermodynamics and a measured K_D — and these predictions were run after it, never into it. Read views 11 and 12 as two negative results: the models do not agree with each other, and the one specificity check with a known right answer gets it wrong.
From cofold_summary.json: These co-folds are FIGURES AND A WEAK SPECIFICITY SIGNAL, NOT RANKING INPUT. The aptamer pipeline deliberately does not rank on predicted structure. CASP16's 27-nt DNA aptamer target had 0 of 107 submitted models under 10 A RMSD; AF3 averages 1.45 A on aptamers published before its training cutoff vs 6.40 A after it; only 35.6% of AF3 protein-nucleic-acid predictions recover more than half the native contacts. Treat cross-model agreement as the signal, never a single model's own confidence score.
⚠ The co-folded constructs are stale — do not compare them to views 3–9. They were snapshotted before the ensemble-ΔG and K_closed corrections and before mismatch tuning existed. construct1, the top-ranked construct then, is 94 nt at K_D,app 971 nM; the 5 constructs here span 72–99 nt and 886–984 nM. The library now reaches 91 nt at 108 nM (switch construct DS CCCTCTTGA at window 10-18) and 54 nt at 125 nM (switch construct DS CTCTTG at window 11-16) — 40 nt shorter than construct1 and still tighter than every chain co-folded here. Same pipeline, different molecules: every structure below is of a sequence the shortlist has since moved past.
⚠ opendde returns a near-constant ipTM (0.63–0.69) whatever you feed it. Across all 6 DNA chains its interface confidence moves by 0.05, while it is also the model that agrees least with the others (mean tolerant Jaccard 0.210 against the other three). It is the most confident model and the least concordant one. A confidence score that does not vary with its input is not carrying information about the input — read it as a warning sign, not a strength.
⚠ ipTM collapses with tether length, which is most likely an artefact rather than worse binding. Boltz-2 scores 0.581 on the bare 45-nt parent and 0.173–0.367 on the 72–99-nt constructs. The difference is mostly 27–54 nt of single-stranded poly-T spacer being scored: it has no defined conformation, so whatever the model draws there is arbitrary and it drags the interface score down by existing. Compare constructs with constructs; never parent against construct.

11 · Cross-model agreement — where four models put the DNA on IL-6

One lane per structure-prediction model, along the IL-6 mature chain as a residue axis. A mark is an IL-6 residue with at least one heavy atom within 4.0 Å of any DNA atom in that model's predicted complex — measured from the returned coordinates, not a score the model reports. The strip underneath counts how many models call each residue, and ▲ marks the residues all three of the converging models agree on. The matrices are the same contact sets as pairwise Jaccard overlap, exact and allowing ±2 residues (two models can hit the same patch and still score near zero if their lists are offset by a residue or two).

⚠ The four models do not agree on where the aptamer binds, so the binding mode is unresolved. Mean pairwise Jaccard of the contact residues is 0.127–0.180 (0.211–0.324 allowing ±2 residues), and at most 1 residue out of unions of 34–82 is called by all four. Some pairs share nothing at all: boltz2 vs opendde, esmfold2 vs opendde score exactly 0.000. Three of them — boltz2 + esmfold2 + protenix — do broadly converge on two patches, and those recurring residues are the obvious thing to probe experimentally, but three models that share training data and biases are correlated evidence, not independent replication.
Table view — per-model confidence, contact count and patches

12 · Off-target panels — the specificity metric fails its own control

Boltz-2 ipTM for one DNA chain against IL-6 and the four other gp130-family cytokines, same model and same protocol throughout. Two chains, two panels, one shared scale. The dashed rule in each panel is the on-target IL-6 value; an off-target bar that crosses it is the model preferring a cytokine the aptamer is not known to bind.

⚠ The metric ranks a known non-target above the known target. For parent45 — the only chain here with a real measured affinity (K_D 27 nM for IL-6 by SPR, and no measurable binding to human serum albumin) — boltz2 scores CNTF 0.597 against IL-6 0.581. The true target comes second of the 5 cytokines, behind one the aptamer is not known to bind, by 0.016 ipTM. This is a negative result about the method, not specificity data: because the metric fails the one case where the right answer is known, the IL-11 margin of +0.019 on construct1 carries no information either — it is well inside the error the control just demonstrated.
⚠ Do not quote any number in this view as specificity. The design is the most defensible thing here — same model, same DNA, same protocol, five homologous cytokines, so systematic errors partly cancel — and it still fails. What the panels rule out is the metric as a selection filter; they are not evidence that the aptamer is or is not selective. The two panels do not even agree with each other on the ordering of the off-targets.
Table view — ipTM, margin and contact count for every target
